summary: Re-map EXISTING dashboard-twin objects rows (type '@cinatra-ai/dashboard-artifact:dashboard') onto the canonical Phase-2 scope tuple (epic cinatra#1883 §D7 ACL cutover, issue #1898). One-shot convergence backfill shipped WITH its code cutover, which removes the Phase-1 dual authorization so the single canonical object.read filter becomes the sole gate for dashboard-typed rows. Two idempotent UPDATEs over objects, dashboard-twins only (every other object row untouched): (1) a project-scoped twin (project_id NOT NULL) is re-owned to owner_level='organization', owner_id=org_id, visibility='private' (project_id kept) so the filter admits it ONLY via the project clause — closing the leak where a twin still carrying owner_level='team'/'user' (the old conservative floor kept the tier verbatim) would be admitted by the visibility-INDEPENDENT owner clause to team members / the owner without a project grant; (2) a workspace-owned unscoped twin (project_id NULL, owner_level='workspace') flips visibility='private'->'public' (org-local public) so it does not DISAPPEAR from the library once the dual gate is gone. team/organization/user unscoped rows already matched the canonical tuple and are excluded. DESTRUCTIVE (data rewrite over an existing table): each UPDATE's IS DISTINCT FROM guards make it idempotent (a second run matches zero rows), a fresh bootstrap has no dashboard twins (no-op, ledger-faked), and a fail-loud postcondition RAISEs (rolling back) if any project-scoped twin still carries a user/team owner clause. No version bump / Graphiti re-projection (a dashboard twin is never projected). down() is IRREVERSIBLE (throws): re-owning overwrites the original owner tier and a re-mapped workspace twin is indistinguishable from a natively-public one — same class as core__0033 / core__0064; restore from a backup to roll back. SEQ 0082 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0080_dashboard-entity-links, #1897) and clears core__0081 (CLAIMED by open PR #2061); a concurrent lane landing an intervening seq first makes a rename-only renumber normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train; the runner tolerates sequence gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
